blocks.text: For the vocal interpretation of the texts, we worked with voice actors to give the texts a voice without claiming to recover the voices of those who wrote them. The letters and archival fragments became spoken (embodied), sometimes fragile, and present through a present-day performance. Their voices mediated the texts, making fragmentary traces audible while always keeping visible the distance between archival evidence and reconstruction.
"There is something about sound and specifically the voice, that carries a more intimate, engaging quality." — Tzlil

blocks.text: "Selecting and arranging the vocalized archival fragments was itself an act of directing. By deciding which voices would be heard, in what order, and in relation to one another, Ari was effectively directing the characters within the imagined auditory space." — Tzlil
